answer: Comet-Kernel Coordination Pricing** Each agent must sumbit a recurrent kernel function whose depth gates how many distinct counterparties it can transact with per epoch. To wander into new coalition space, an agent posts a precision bond that is slashed if its kernel output diverges from observed behavior. Sybil clusters pay the bond per identity, and pay again each time they merge, so coordination itself becomes the priced resource: the attacker's cost scales with every extra node it must synchronize.
